title: 1993 AHSME Problem 13
statement: A square of perimeter \(20\) is inscribed in a square of perimeter \(28.\) What is the greatest distance between a vertex of the inner square and a vertex of the outer square?

solutions.text: The outer and inner side lengths are \(7\) and \(5.\) At any inner vertex, the two pieces of the outer side have lengths \(x\) and \(y\) with \[ x+y=7,\qquad x^2+y^2=25. \] Hence \(2xy=49-25=24,\) so \(\{x,y\}=\{3,4\}.\) From an inner vertex on one side, the farther opposite outer vertex has horizontal displacement \(4\) and vertical displacement \(7.\) The greatest distance is therefore \(\sqrt{4^2+7^2}=\sqrt{65}.\) Thus the correct answer is D.
hints: A vertex of the inner square divides an outer side into lengths \(x\) and \(y\)
